text: Reduce fetch_sitemap double DNS resolution: validate_sitemap_url currently resolves (advisory) and http.fetch_page resolves again (authoritative, pinning). Not a TOCTOU - the second resolution is the one that pins - but it doubles resolver load per sitemap fetch and permits ~2x DNS amplification on an attacker-controlled hostname. Proposal: reduce validate_sitemap_url to a deterministic preflight (scheme, host presence, metadata hostnames, IP-literal classification) and leave hostname resolution solely to fetch_page; or rename the resolving variant so it cannot be mistaken for authorization. Flagged by 057-S adversarial review (Security P3, Architecture P2). Grounded: src/docline/fetch/sitemap.py validate_sitemap_url + fetch_sitemap.

Split src/docline/fetch/crawl.py (now ~660 lines, past the 400-line module convention) and extract frontier bookkeeping into a module-level private dataclass with an admit() method, replacing the _admit/_report_ceiling closures and their nonlocal state so the admission rule is unit-testable without driving a full crawl. Raised as P2 by the Python-safety persona during 058-S review and declined there to keep the shipment diff surgical; crawl.py already exceeded the ceiling before 058-S. Source: docs/closure/2026-08-29-058-s-crawl-frontier-bound-closure.md

Surface crawl frontier truncation downstream. A ceiling hit is currently signalled only by one DEBUG record, so elt/execute.py writes crawl-manifest.json from a silently truncated CrawlResult list and a partial crawl is indistinguishable from a complete one on both the CLI and MCP paths. WebCrawlSource leaves max_pages unbounded, so a legitimate large crawl past MAX_FRONTIER=10000 admissions can truncate with no user-visible signal. Promote the drop record to a level operators see by default and add a frontier_truncated marker to the staged manifest. The reviewed 058-S plan explicitly deferred any counter field or CrawlResult marker, so this is accepted risk carried forward, not a defect. Source: docs/closure/2026-08-29-058-s-crawl-frontier-bound-closure.md

Prioritise mdBook TOC-derived links over in-page anchors when the crawl frontier ceiling truncates. At depth zero _discover_toc_links results are appended to the tail of discovered_links, so an append-time cap drops authoritative TOC navigation first on exactly the sites where the TOC is the canonical page set. Inert below the default ceiling; only matters in the adversarial or very-large-crawl regime. Raised as P3 by the correctness persona during 058-S review. Source: docs/closure/2026-08-29-058-s-crawl-frontier-bound-closure.md
